themes.theme: Interest rate tensions and yield curve

arguments.conclusion: Lowering short-term rates to please Trump will lead to higher long-term rates due to increased money supply and inflation expectations.
premises: The US government borrows and spends more when short-term rates are low
Borrowing and spending increases the money supply
Increased money supply causes prices to rise
Rational lenders demand higher long-term rates to compensate for inflation
Long-term rates have been heading higher recently despite short-term cuts

evidence.item: Money supply at an all-time high
evidence.verification_basis: transcript provides the assertion as a datum
evidence.source_speech_filename: 20260202_Kevin Warsh New Fed Chair will Change EVERYTHING.txt
evidence.source_excerpt: money supply... is now sitting at an all-time high

evidence.item: Long-term rates like 20-year and 30-year Treasury yields heading higher
evidence.verification_basis: transcript provides this observation as fact
evidence.source_speech_filename: 20260202_Kevin Warsh New Fed Chair will Change EVERYTHING.txt
evidence.source_excerpt: you look at long-term interest rates like the yield on the 20-year Treasury or the 30-year Treasury, they've actually been heading higher

arguments.conclusion: Removing the supplementary leverage ratio and providing an implicit Fed backstop will enable banks to buy unlimited US Treasuries, allowing long-term rates to stay low.
premises: The supplementary leverage ratio restricts banks' Treasury purchases
There is a push to deregulate, especially from Governor Steven Moran
The Fed's Bank Term Funding Program allows banks to sell Treasuries back to the Fed at full price
Banks care only about the spread between what they pay depositors and what they earn on Treasuries
An implicit bailout makes Treasuries effectively risk-free for banks

evidence.item: Supplementary leverage ratio limits Treasury holdings
evidence.source_speech_filename: 20260202_Kevin Warsh New Fed Chair will Change EVERYTHING.txt
evidence.source_excerpt: a restriction on how many treasuries banks can buy because the rules right now regulating banks say that treasuries are risky

evidence.item: Bank Term Funding Program temporarily buys treasuries at full price
evidence.source_speech_filename: 20260202_Kevin Warsh New Fed Chair will Change EVERYTHING.txt
evidence.source_excerpt: the Federal Reserve already has a tool to deal with that called the bank term funding program. If treasuries do go down in value, banks can temporarily sell those treasuries back to the Fed for full price

arguments.conclusion: Fed chairs often act contrary to their prior rhetoric when faced with economic pressure, so Kevin Warsh will likely continue expansionary policies.
